items.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
items.description: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said. A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night. Banda Daud Shah and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendents of police (DSP) led the operation, in which bomb disposal unit (BDU) personnel, a drone team, Rescue 15 personnel and Rapid Response Force personnel also participated, the statement said. “During the operation, the law enforcers raided the hideout of a terrorist commander, Qaiser Iqbal, where an exchange of fire took place,” the police said, adding that two terrorists were killed in the encounter. CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan, Latambar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector (SI) Afzal Awan, Constable Kazim and Head Constable Amjad from the BDU were martyred in the exchange of fire. The statement said the operation was ongoing. It added, “The brave martyred personnel of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police have set a shining example of dedication to duty, courage, and a commitment to public safety by sacrificing their lives in the fight against terrorism.” The statement said the sacrifices of the martyred policemen reflected the police force’s “unwavering resolve” to continue making every possible effort to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace in the region. Later, the funeral prayers for the martyred police personnel were offered with full official honours. According to the KP police, the funeral was attended by KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed, CTD Additional IG Jawad Qamar, Kohat Regional Police Officer Shakir Hussain Dawar, Kohat Commissioner Parvez Khan Sabt Khel, CTD Senior Superintendent of Police (Operations) Najamul Hasnain, Karak Deputy Commissioner Hamid Iqbal and Karak District Police Officer Niaz Muhammad, among other high-ranking civil and military and police officers, the families of the martyred personnel, and others. A police contingent presented a final salute to the martyrs, while high-ranking officers paid tribute to them by laying floral wreaths on their coffins. “The attendees honoured the supreme sacrifices offered by the martyrs, prayed for the elevation of their ranks, and sought patience for the bereaved families,” the police statement added. Police officers pay tribute to the martyred police personnel during funeral prayers in KP’s Karak on Oct 22. — photo courtesy KP police KP IGP Hameed paid tributes to the bravery, sense of duty, and professional commitment of the martyrs. He stressed the great courage of the KP police personnel in laying down their lives while confronting terrorists. “The martyrs’ bravery, unwavering dedication to duty, and unparalleled sacrifices for the protection of the public serve as a guiding light for the entire police force,” he added. Earlier, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the incident and expressed sorrow over the martyrdom of four police personnel. “The sacrifices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police in the fight against terrorism are unforgettable. The blood of our martyrs will not go to waste; our resolve against terrorism will be further strengthened, and the struggle for the establishment of peace will continue,” he said in an X post. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time, including attacks on police personnel. Thursday’s operation comes around 20 days after several terrorist hideouts were destroyed during a joint search and strike operation in Karak. In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

items.title: Manifestations en France : Bitchat, la messagerie sans réseau qui a le vent en poupe
items.description: En pleine mobilisation lycéenne et pour le pouvoir d'achat en France, Bitchat mesh se classait n°1, jeudi, des applications sur l'App Store dans la catégorie "réseaux sociaux". Lancée en juillet 2025 par le cofondateur de Twitter, cette messagerie décentralisée fonctionne avec le Bluetooth et sans Internet. Pratique quand le réseau est saturé, comme cela peut arriver dans une manifestation.

items.title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
items.description: Turkiye will host an R-4 and an R-4+E-3 meeting of foreign ministers in Istanbul on October 23, the Turkish foreign ministry said on Thursday. The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran. The E-3 group is a trio of European powers — France, Britain and Germany — that was set up more than 20 years ago to advance diplomatic coordination over Iran’s nuclear programme. The Foreign Office in Islamabad has yet to comment on the planned meetings and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s participation. A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran , Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security. The ministers are expected to discuss the Israeli-Palestinian issue, the latest situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and opportunities for closer cooperation between the regional and European countries, the source added. Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, they said. Fidan will also tell counterparts that Turkiye has been working to stop the war in Ukraine from spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source said.

items.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives. The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966. PM Shehbaz said, “I want to say that connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Islamabad or Karachi, so this air link is very important. “I have already given instructions to our ministry of civil aviation to prepare a quick feasibility [study], be it Pakistan International Airlines, or any other airline in Pakistan, to find the ways and means to take the first flight comprising tourists [and the] business community to Malé,” he announced. The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that he gave instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”. “I have given instructions to our civil aviation department to immediately invite a delegation from [the] Maldives and work out a plan whereby we can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” PM Shehbaz added. Moreover, the premier highlighted the importance of maritime connectivity, noting that unless there is a reliable direct shipping schedule from Karachi or Gwadar to Malé, “we will not be able to meet our targets efficiently and effectively.” He added that once Muizzu returned to his country, a delegation of Pakistani government officials and businessmen would be sent to Malé. He said that the delegation would arrive within the next week or so. Calling Muizzu a “very sincere friend of Pakistan”, the premier hailed his visit as a “turning point in further strengthening our bilateral, brotherly relations” and a “game-changer in terms of promoting our bilateral trade and investment portfolios”. “I would like to convey this message to our great entrepreneurs, traders, investors and businessmen from both [the] Maldives and Pakistan,” he added. “Here is an opportunity we can really convert into … a concrete action plan.” Citing figures provided by Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, PM Shehbaz said that the trade volume between Islamabad and Malé is approximately $13 million. “My brother, President Dr Muizzu, on my request, readily agreed to make a firm understanding to increase our bilateral trade from $13m to $200m in the next two years, and now it’s all up to us to make use of this opportunity, do our homework and make full preparation to achieve these targets through joint efforts and very close coordination,” the prime minister stated. Taking the podium, President Muizzu echoed PM Shehbaz and urged the establishment of an air corridor between Pakistan and the Maldives. “In this regard, I am pleased to announce that Maldivian, our national airline, aims to establish [a] direct air link between Malé and Karachi soon,” he announced. “This service will make travel easier for the people of our two countries, creating new opportunities for trade and tourism.” He thanked PM Shehbaz for taking the time to attend the forum and said that his presence was “a testament to the close friendship and our shared commitment to strengthening economic cooperation”. “It is such a great pleasure for me to be with you today in Islamabad. And particularly to address a gathering of those who drive enterprise, investment, and economic opportunity in our two countries,” he added. “As we mark 60 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the relationship between the Maldives and Pakistan is rooted in deep fraternal affection, and above all, in the enduring bond of our Islamic faith.” Muizzu noted that while Islamabad and Malé had strong political solidarity and diplomatic trust, their economic relationship had yet to reach its full potential. “We must now define the ambition of our future,” the Maldivian president said. “The time has come to transform the strength of our friendship into a new era of trade, investment, and shared prosperity, which is why yesterday Prime Minister Sharif and I agreed to enhance our bilateral trade to $200m over the next two years.” He added, “Beyond the numbers, this ambitious target is investing in our people. We are not only creating new opportunities for businesses on both sides, but also fostering greater regional prosperity and long-term stability.” Muizzu said Pakistan possessed tremendous potential and that the economies of both nations had “important complementarities”. “For the Maldives, food security is not merely a commercial consideration. As an island nation, resilient supply chains are a matter of national security, and the scale of our market should not be underestimated,” he explained. Noting that Pakistan’s agricultural sector already serves the island nation, Muizzu emphasised the need to move beyond a typical buyer and seller relationship into partnerships in cold chain logistics, temperature-controlled storage, modern food processing and climate-adaptive agricultural technology. “But trade requires connectivity. For an island nation, maritime connectivity is an economic lifeline. We must create more efficient corridors through which that trade can move,” he highlighted. “Therefore, I encourage shipping, port and logistics companies from both countries to explore direct and commercially viable connections between Pakistan and the Maldives.” Stressing the importance of healthcare infrastructure, the Maldivian president highlighted that the country is making significant investments to move from regional tertiary hospitals to modern island-level facilities. “Our demand for reliable, high-quality and certified medical supplies will therefore continue to grow. We welcome Pakistani pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare providers,” Muizzu said. Furthermore, he invited Pakistan’s construction companies, developers, manufacturers and engineering firms to partner with the Maldives in housing, land reclamation and connectivity projects, as part of Malé’s endeavours in infrastructure and urban development. “Renewable energy is another area of enormous potential. The Maldives spends hundreds of millions of dollars each year importing diesel. For us, therefore, the transition to clean energy is not only a climate imperative, it is an economic and fiscal necessity,” he added. “My administration has set a target of producing 33 per cent of our national electricity requirement from renewable sources by 2028. That means more than quadrupling more than the amount generated in a five-year period.” Additionally, the Maldivian president highlighted opportunities in both nations, unlocking the power of the global Islamic economy through Sharia-compliant finance, and halal tourism and products. “The Maldives is strengthening its financial landscape and institutional frameworks for Islamic finance,” he said. “Together, our financial institutions, regulators, and businesses can explore Sharia-compliant investment instruments, sukuk , Islamic financial services and halal value chains. And these areas are by no means exhaustive.” Muizzu also highlighted opportunities in tourism and hospitality, IT, education and other sectors and invited Pakistani businesses to “not look at the Maldives merely as a market to sell to, [but] look at the Maldives as a partner to build with”. Later, the Maldivian president expressed his gratitude to PM Shehbaz for his presence at the business forum and for “highlighting the key priorities that will guide our economic partnership into a new chapter”. In a post on X, he said that the forum marked an important first step towards realising the ambition of increasing bilateral trade over the next two years. “I warmly invite Pakistani businesses and investors to explore the wealth of opportunities the Maldives has to offer,” Muizzu said, stating his confidence that the renewed commitment would “forge meaningful partnerships, attract investment, and deliver tangible benefits” to both Pakistan and the Maldives. “Let us build an economic partnership that reflects the strength of our enduring friendship, one that creates opportunities for our peoples, advances shared prosperity, and translates our common aspirations into lasting progress,” he added.

À Saly, la CPE passe sous présidence guinéenne et fixe le cap pour la gestion des barrages [Par Aboubacar Sakho]
items.description: La 156ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la Commission permanente des eaux (CPE) de l’Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS) s’est tenue les 20 et 21 octobre 2026 à Saly, au Sénégal. Cette rencontre a réuni les représentants des États membres, du Haut-Commissariat, du Comité de bassin, ainsi que des sociétés de gestion et d’exploitation des ouvrages communs, notamment la SOGED, la SOGEM, la SOGENAV et la SEMAF-SA. Au cœur des travaux figuraient le bilan de la gestion des barrages de Manantali, de Gouina, de Félou et de Diama, l’examen des programmes d’exploitation pour la fin de l’année 2026, ainsi que plusieurs enjeux environnementaux et agricoles liés à la gestion des ressources en eau du bassin du fleuve Sénégal. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été marquée par le passage de témoin entre le Sénégal et la Guinée à la tête de la Commission permanente des eaux. Conformément à l’article 8 du règlement intérieur de la CPE, amendé par la résolution n° 00407 du 21 décembre 2004, la République de Guinée assure désormais la présidence de cette instance pour une durée d’un an, succédant ainsi à la République du Sénégal. La passation s’est déroulée entre M. Moussa BERTHE, représentant le Coordonnateur de la Cellule nationale OMVS/OMVG du Sénégal, et Mme Hawa TRAORE, représentant le Coordonnateur de la Cellule nationale OMVS de Guinée. À cette occasion, les participants ont salué la qualité de la présidence sénégalaise et adressé leurs félicitations à l’équipe sortante. Ils ont également exprimé leurs encouragements à la Guinée pour la réussite de son nouveau mandat. Après les mots de bienvenue de M. Moussa BERTHE, le Secrétaire général de l’OMVS, M. Niokhor NDOUR, a félicité l’ensemble des acteurs du système pour leur implication constante dans les travaux de la Commission. Il a souligné le caractère déterminant de cet engagement collectif pour améliorer durablement la gestion des ressources en eau du bassin du fleuve Sénégal. La cérémonie a également été empreinte de recueillement à la suite du rappel à Dieu de M. Djibril NDAW, chauffeur mécanicien au Haut-Commissariat de l’OMVS. Des prières ont été formulées en sa mémoire. Les travaux ont permis d’examiner l’état d’exécution des recommandations des précédentes réunions, ainsi que le bilan du programme de gestion des barrages arrêté lors de la 155ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la CPE. À l’issue des échanges, la Commission a constaté que les programmes de gestion des barrages de Manantali, de Gouina, de Félou et de Diama avaient été globalement respectés. Pour le barrage de Manantali, les lâchers d’eau avaient notamment été programmés afin de garantir, à Bakel, des débits minimaux répondant aux besoins en aval, notamment pour l’agriculture, les consommations humaines et animales et la navigation. La réunion a également permis de faire le point sur les objectifs de production d’énergie hydroélectrique fixés pour 2026. Les productibles annuels adoptés s’élèvent à 915 GWh pour Manantali, 583,348 GWh pour Gouina et 299,462 GWh pour Félou. Ces objectifs traduisent la volonté de concilier les besoins en eau des populations et des activités économiques avec les impératifs de production énergétique, dans un contexte où la gestion coordonnée des ouvrages demeure essentielle à l’équilibre du bassin À l’issue de l’examen des propositions soumises par le Haut-Commissariat, la SOGED, la SOGEM et la SEMAF-SA, la CPE a adopté les programmes de gestion des barrages pour la période allant du 22 octobre au 31 décembre 2026. La Commission a par ailleurs examiné les présentations de la Direction nationale du génie rural de Guinée (DNGR), de l’Agence de développement rural de la vallée du fleuve Sénégal (ADRS), de la Société nationale pour le développement rural (SONADER) et de la Société nationale d’aménagement et d’exploitation des terres du delta du fleuve Sénégal et des vallées du fleuve Sénégal et de la Falémé (SAED). Ces communications ont porté sur les superficies mises en valeur et les productions agricoles de 2026, les prévisions d’emblavures pour 2027 ainsi que les mesures d’entretien des axes hydrauliques. En prenant acte des activités réalisées par les sociétés d’aménagement hydro-agricole, la CPE s’est félicitée des efforts accomplis et les a encouragées à consolider les acquis. Ces actions restent essentielles pour soutenir la production agricole, améliorer la maîtrise de l’eau et préserver le bon fonctionnement des infrastructures hydrauliques Au terme de deux jours de travaux, la 156ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la Commission permanente des eaux a permis de consolider les orientations relatives à la gestion coordonnée des barrages, à la production hydroélectrique et à la préservation des ressources naturelles du bassin. La prochaine réunion de la CPE est prévue à Conakry, en Guinée, au cours de la deuxième quinzaine de décembre 2026. Elle se tiendra sous la présidence guinéenne, dans la continuité des efforts engagés par les États membres et les structures de l’OMVS pour une gestion concertée, durable et solidaire des eaux du fleuve Sénégal. Aboubacar SAKHO Expert en Communication au Haut-Commissariat de l’OMVS à Dakar L’article À Saly, la CPE passe sous présidence guinéenne et fixe le cap pour la gestion des barrages [Par Aboubacar Sakho] est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

Inscrite à l’Institut supérieur des études technologiques (Iset) de Sfax, la jeune fille a été victime d’un malaise dans la nuit du mercredi 21 octobre dernier. Dans son communiqué, l'UGET réclame des solutions durables pour garantir l'accès immédiat aux soins et exhorte les autorités de tutelle à assumer leurs responsabilités en prenant des mesures d'urgence pour préserver la vie des étudiants. items.title: Sudan lifts ban on 46 imports as inflation rises and Dollar hits SDG 10,300
items.description: Sudan has lifted import restrictions on 46 goods as the Dollar climbs to SDG 10,300 and annual inflation reaches 28.29%, deepening pressure on consumers already struggling with soaring food prices. Sudan’s Sovereignty Council chairman Abdelfattah El Burhan has cancelled a cabinet decision banning imports of 46 goods, as Sudan’s currency and consumers remain under pressure from rising prices. Finance minister Jibril Ibrahim says the decision takes account of consumers’ needs while providing measures to protect domestic producers. Traders and consumers have reported an immediate fall in some prices following the announcement. Vegetables at Khartoum Central Market (File photo: Supplied) The National Importers’ Chamber welcomed the move but called for Prime Minister Kamil Idris to issue a clear, enforceable decision cancelling Resolution No. 74, which introduced the restrictions. The chamber’s chairman, El Sadiq Jalal El Din Saleh, said the import ban had disrupted markets and caused substantial losses to importers. However, foreign-exchange dealers reported that the Dollar rose on Thursday to SDG 10,200 for buying and SDG 10,300 for selling, an increase of SDG 100 from Wednesday. Experts expect further increases, particularly following the lifting of the import restrictions. Inflation and food prices rise Sudan’s annual inflation rate rose to 28.29% in September, up from 26.14% in August, while monthly inflation reached 7.5%, according to the Central Bureau of Statistics. Food and drink prices rose by 17.26% during the month, with annual inflation in the category reaching 36.81%. Annual inflation was significantly higher in urban areas, at 40.35%, than in rural areas, at 21.18%. War compounds economic crisis Economists attribute rising inflation to the destruction of Sudan’s productive base during the war, growing dependence on imports, the depreciation of the pound, and the use of the customs Dollar to calculate duties. Taxes, customs charges, and transport costs have added to the burden. The conflict has also prevented many people from returning to agricultural and other productive areas, restricting domestic supplies. Markets remain fragmented between areas controlled by the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, while production and supply chains have yet to recover. The latest figures point to a difficult economic balance: easing import restrictions may improve the availability of goods, but the continuing rise in the Dollar and the cost of food threaten to erode any relief for consumers. items.title: Burkina: 2 800 milliards FCFA pour «l’Énergie pour Tous» dans 10 ans
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 22 octobre 2026). Le Conseil des Ministres s'est réuni ce jeudi, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, Président du Conseil des Ministres. Selon le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ assurant l’Intérim du Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Conseil a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour et pris des décisions importantes pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création de l'Initiative Présidentielle Énergie pour Tous « Faso Wa-Fulu », en langue nationale san. Portée par le Ministère en charge de l'Énergie, cette initiative d'envergure nationale vise à garantir un accès généralisé à l'électricité d'ici à 2030. D’un coût de plus de 2 800 milliards FCFA sur 10 ans, le programme s'articule autour de 4 composantes que sont les Brigades d'électrification, l’Inclusion communautaire, l’Accès énergétique et la Souveraineté énergétique. « Cette initiative vise à accélérer l’accès de l'énergie pour tous à l'horizon 2030. C'est une initiative qui va s'étaler sur une période de 10 ans, avec une première période d'accélération de la prise en charge des questions énergétiques et une seconde phase de 5 ans qui sera consacrée à la consolidation des acquis », a expliqué le Ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA. Naissance de la Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB) Au titre du Ministère de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création d’une société d'économie mixte à participation publique majoritaire dénommée Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB). Pour le Ministre du Commerce, de l'Industrie et de l'Artisanat, le Camarade Serge Gnaniodem PODA, cette société d'économie mixte est dotée d'un capital initial d’un milliard FCFA avec une participation de 45 % pour l’État, 10 % pour BRAFASO et 45 % pour le secteur privé burkinabè. « La SOVIB permettra la création de centaines d’emplois et la transformation de vignes produites au Burkina Faso », a soutenu le Ministre PODA. Cette unité industrielle sera basée à Bobo-Dioulasso, et nécessitera un investissement d'environ 9,8 milliards FCFA. items.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
items.description: England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday. The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India’s Shubman Gill. In the process, Brook also eclipsed England’s highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. Brook’s scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England’s innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage. England’s captain Harry Brook celebrates after scoring a double century (200 runs) during the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — AFP He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd. The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. “Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn’t matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn’t even count,” Brook said. “Heart-breaking. I think you’ve hit the nail on the head there. It’s very disappointing that we haven’t been able to defend 430, but that’s life, that’s cricket,” he added. “You don’t see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They’ve played exceptionally well. We couldn’t execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they’ve just played an absolute blinder there. “We’ll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We’ve got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore.” Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls as England piled up 429-4. But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries. Sri Lanka’s Pavan Rathnayake in action in the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — Reuters Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook’s record-breaking innings all in vain. Tongue was England’s most successful bowler with 3-79. England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi on Tuesday to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.

items.title: A Congressional District Where the Iran War Is Personal
items.description: J ohn Quillin thought America’s Middle Eastern wars were safely in the past. He spent two decades in the Navy, enlisting not long before the September 11 attacks and retiring as a chief petty officer about 18 months after the United States withdrew from Afghanistan. “Now we’re right back in it,” he told me, “and it’s taking a huge toll on everybody.” I met Quillin as he handed out Democratic sample ballots outside an early-voting location in Chesapeake, Virginia. He is one of more than 80,000 veterans—along with more than 30,000 active-duty and reserve personnel—who live in Virginia’s Second Congressional District, where the debate over the Iran war is about far more than rising gas prices. The district wraps around Naval Station Norfolk, home of the Navy’s Fleet Forces Command. Since 2008, the seat has toggled between the major parties four times, and the results have mirrored overall House control. Polls show a tight race with money pouring in from both sides. Both Jen Kiggans, the Republican incumbent, and Elaine Luria, the Democratic challenger, are veterans who have centered their campaigns on the military, but in very different ways. Luria, a former Navy commander, is telling voters that the conflict in Iran has needlessly weakened the military and is endangering strategic goals in other parts of the world. Iran is a war of choice, she argues, that is taking a toll on service members through extended deployments, even as costs balloon and the timeline for bringing it to a close keeps shifting. People are worried about their friends and family members on active duty, she told me, and are “concerned about the fact that we are running the fleet into the ground.” Kiggans, a former naval-helicopter pilot, presents herself as a candidate who can work with the opposing party, and she has broken with the administration to champion an offshore wind development. But she is putting no distance between herself and Trump on the war, echoing his insistence that America must prevent Iran from having a nuclear weapon. Kiggans told the Associated Press last week that Luria has “chosen the side of Iran” and that “it’s like the Democrats are now siding with the Iranians and not standing with our military.” Many Republican voters in the district told me they agree with her support for Trump’s war, and are willing to endure temporary hardships if it means long-term success. Lance Lesher, a Navy veteran and the chairman of the Republican Party of Virginia Beach, told me that Iran has been at war with the United States since the country’s 1979 revolution—and that Trump was right to act when he did. “I mean, high prices for gasoline—no one likes that,” the 59-year-old Lesher told me. “I think most people, though, at least most older people, have the perspective—is it worth it? Is it worth paying $5 a gallon for gasoline for six months for Iran to not have a nuclear weapon?” L uria is wagering that undecided voters who are now paying more to fill their gas tanks and grocery carts won’t agree with that premise. At a meet and greet in Suffolk, Elisha Harris, a pioneering local football coach, started a call-and-response that summed up Luria’s pitch: “Gas was three-fifty. Now it’s over four. Diesel hit a record. We can’t take much more. Every fill-up’s a drain—” “It ain’t been the same, without Elaine!” the crowd responded. [ Read: Trump is considering a plan to strike Iran before the midterms ] Luria was first elected in 2018, turning the district blue amid an anti-Trump wave. She held the seat two years later, but Kiggans then beat her by three points in 2022 after tying the Democrat to the Biden administration’s disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan. Luria is now hoping to return the favor, by capitalizing on the unpopularity of Trump’s foreign policy. Kiggans sits on the House Armed Services Committee, which has not held a public hearing on the Iran war since May 19. Calls for greater House oversight surged this spring amid reports of deteriorating conditions aboard aircraft carriers, including the Norfolk-based USS Gerald Ford, which took part in the opening days of the conflict. The carrier returned to Virginia in May after an 11-month deployment that was beset by plumbing issues and a fire that left hundreds of sailors without a place to sleep. When asked in March about the ship’s reported maintenance issues, Kiggans told a local news station that she was concerned about them, but that “this is not Carnival Cruise—this is the U.S. Navy.” It’s a line Luria repeats often, claiming that Kiggans has failed to provide oversight as the war degrades military readiness and needlessly endangers lives. “I know the number of veterans in this room who have served in uniform, like I have. And we have our sailors deploying in harm’s way,” Luria told the crowd in Suffolk. “The lack of sensitivity and compassion, her inability, on the Armed Services Committee, to stand up and ask tough questions of our military leadership—I mean, the silence is deafening.” The idea that Congress has abdicated oversight of the military repeatedly came up in my conversations with Democratic voters across the district. Many said that they were proud of their service and hold the military in the highest regard, but that patriotism also means criticizing the country and pointing out its mistakes. Mike Carter, who spent years flying F/A-18 Super Hornets, told me he’d come to the Luria event because he worried that the military and country were losing global respect. Marsha Simmons, who cast an early ballot for Luria, told me that her husband served in the Navy, and she worried that today’s Department of Defense was not taking national security seriously enough. Donna Grieco said that she loved her eight years working as a Navy nurse, and that the experience made her especially concerned about the long deployments sailors are enduring. “I don’t agree with the war,” she told me. “And I feel like the demands we are putting on our sailors—it’s not necessary.” N ot every veteran sees it that way. Over Mike Cassidy’s 22-year Navy career, he sailed the Baltic Sea and helped fight ISIS. He was deployed five times to the Persian Gulf. Cassidy’s service convinced him that American adversaries such as Iran need to be confronted. “I know what we’ve been up against in that part of the world,” he told me at a Republican Party barbecue. “I can tell you that we’re doing the right thing.” [ Read: Trump is preparing for a long war ] At 9 a.m. on a Saturday, the Lockside Bar and Grill in Chesapeake was packed with people decked out in glittery hats and red, white, and blue. Kiggans stood at a podium flanked by two American flags. “My oldest just had his first flight in an F/A-18 this week!” she announced. People whooped. “So many of us have family members that serve, and have kids that we’re leaving this great country to,” she went on. “It is the greatest country in the world. We’ve got to keep it that way.” At times, the rally seemed less about Kiggans than about Trump. His core supporters cheered when Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio took the stage and recited a list of MAGA world’s greatest hits: the Steele dossier, Jack Smith, Fani Willis. “Thanks for helping the president,” Jordan said to applause. “Talk about someone doing what he said he would do.” Kiggans has voted six times against resolutions that would have directed Trump to end the war with Iran. She declined an interview request, but in April, she said on a conservative talk-radio show that she “couldn’t be a stauncher supporter” of military action against Iran. When I asked the campaign whether she still held that position, Kiggans said in a statement that she wants the war to end quickly, but “Iran has been an enemy of the United States for decades and has been the sponsor of terrorism and terrorists around the world who have killed or injured thousands of Americans. Iran can never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.” The race will likely hinge on a small number of voters who have not yet made up their mind. Kiggans knows this and has avoided uncomfortable questions about how the war is going. At an event in Virginia Beach this month with U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Kiggans was asked by a reporter if the war has had an impact on her campaign. A staff member quickly cut in: “We’re not going to talk about that.” *Illustration sources: Peter Casey / The Virginian-Pilot / Tribune News Service / Getty; Nathan Howard / Getty; AFP / Getty; Atta Kenare / AFP / Getty.

items.title: Burkina : Le gouvernement crée l’Initiative Présidentielle Énergie pour Tous « Faso Wa-Fulu »
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 22 octobre 2026). Le Conseil des Ministres s'est réuni ce jeudi, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, Président du Conseil des Ministres. Selon le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ assurant l’Intérim du Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Conseil a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour et pris des décisions importantes pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création de l'Initiative Présidentielle Énergie pour Tous « Faso Wa-Fulu », en langue nationale san. Portée par le Ministère en charge de l'Énergie, cette initiative d'envergure nationale vise à garantir un accès généralisé à l'électricité d'ici à 2030. D’un coût de plus de 2 800 milliards FCFA sur 10 ans, le programme s'articule autour de 4 composantes que sont les Brigades d'électrification, l’Inclusion communautaire, l’Accès énergétique et la Souveraineté énergétique. « Cette initiative vise à accélérer l’accès de l'énergie pour tous à l'horizon 2030. C'est une initiative qui va s'étaler sur une période de 10 ans, avec une première période d'accélération de la prise en charge des questions énergétiques et une seconde phase de 5 ans qui sera consacrée à la consolidation des acquis », a expliqué le Ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA. Naissance de la Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB) Au titre du Ministère de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création d’une société d'économie mixte à participation publique majoritaire dénommée Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB). Pour le Ministre du Commerce, de l'Industrie et de l'Artisanat, le Camarade Serge Gnaniodem PODA, cette société d'économie mixte est dotée d'un capital initial d’un milliard FCFA avec une participation de 45 % pour l’État, 10 % pour BRAFASO et 45 % pour le secteur privé burkinabè. « La SOVIB permettra la création de centaines d’emplois et la transformation de vignes produites au Burkina Faso », a soutenu le Ministre PODA. Cette unité industrielle sera basée à Bobo-Dioulasso, et nécessitera un investissement d'environ 9,8 milliards FCFA. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso Minute.bf

items.title: Des produits agricoles jetés dans la nature : la justice lance une enquête
items.description: La justice se penche sur le phénomène de la spéculation et vise particulièrement une pratique scandaleuse, celle qui consiste à jeter ou détruire des produits alimentaires, notamment la tomate, pour éviter la baisse des prix . Le parquet général près la Cour d’Alger a ordonné l’ouverture d 'enquêtes sur ces pratiques, indique un communiqué de la même juridiction diffusé ce jeudi 22 octobre. Des vidéos montrent des personnes en train de jeter des produits alimentaires Le procureur général a ordonné aux services de police judiciaire relevant des différents corps de sécurité, sous la supervision du Pôle national de lutte contre le crime organisé, d’ouvrir « des enquêtes immédiates, urgentes et exhaustives », à la suite de la diffusion de vidéos sur les réseaux sociaux montrant « des personnes à bord de camions en train de jeter des denrées alimentaires de grande consommation et des légumes de toutes sortes, propres à la consommation, dans des lieux situés en dehors du tissu urbain, dans le but d’empêcher leur distribution, de créer une pénurie sur le marché et de spéculer sur leurs prix », lit-on dans le communiqué. Identifier tout coupable, « quels que soient son statut ou sa fonction » Les enquêtes visent à identifier toute personne ayant participé à ces actes, ayant incité à les commettre, les ayant financés ou en ayant tiré profit, « quels que soient son statut ou sa fonction », précise-t-on. Elles visent aussi à débusquer « les réseaux et les ramifications qui se cachent derrière ces agissements, à retracer les circuits des marchandises ainsi que les réseaux de stockage et de distribution ». Les personnes impliquées seront déférées devant les autorités judiciaires compétentes afin qu’elles soient « poursuivies avec toute la rigueur prévue par la législation en vigueur », conclut la Cour d’Alger. Lors de la réunion du Conseil des ministres de dimanche dernier, le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a ordonné au Premier ministre, Sifi Ghrieb, d’ouvrir des enquêtes sur les pratiques frauduleuses et la spéculation qui entourent les opérations de commercialisation des viandes importées. items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.60 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.64
items.description: The government on Thursday decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.60 per litre, but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.64. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs377.71 per litre while HSD will cost Rs391.75 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 23 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: TRANSLOG Africa 2026 : Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine
items.description: Ouverte le 20 octobre 2026, la 5e édition du Symposium international sur le Transport et la Logistique en Afrique (TRANSLOG Africa) 2026 s’est refermée, ce 21 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. À l’issue des travaux, les participants ont formulé des recommandations visant à maîtriser la chaîne logistique afin de garantir et de renforcer la souveraineté africaine. Ces recommandations s’adressent aux États, aux organisations sous-régionales, aux autorités portuaires, au Conseil burkinabè des chargeurs (CBC) et aux centres de formation. En matière d’information et de digitalisation, le CBC est invité à concevoir et à diffuser la suite du portail de renseignements officiels du système national de gestion. Les participants souhaitent également que les États et les organisations sous-régionales renforcent l’interopérabilité des plateformes numériques ainsi que le partage sécurisé des données entre ports, douanes, escales des corridors et opérateurs privés. Les coûts logistiques ont aussi été examinés. Les autorités portuaires et le CBC sont appelés à analyser les coûts de stationnement dans la chaîne logistique, à identifier les dysfonctionnements et à adopter des mesures correctives appropriées. Les participants ont en outre insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les compétences locales. Les centres de formation supérieure sont invités à développer une expertise nationale en ingénierie des projets d’infrastructures logistiques. Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine -©Faso7 « Vos travaux ont posé un diagnostic lucide : vétusté des infrastructures, insuffisance de la digitalisation et de l’interconnexion des systèmes, guichet unique non opérationnel, persistance de pratiques anormales sur les axes et frais de détention qui alourdissent les coûts logistiques », a déclaré Émile Zerbo, ministre d’État chargé de l’Administration territoriale. Selon le ministre, l’objectif est d’améliorer la performance de la chaîne logistique, de simplifier les procédures et de renforcer la coopération régionale. Pour lui, il n'y a pas de souveraineté véritable sans une maîtrise de la chaîne logistique. Plateforme intergouvernementale Émile Zerbo a exprimé l’engagement du Burkina Faso à assurer le suivi de ces recommandations via un comité dédié et à encadrer juridiquement la reconnaissance de TRANSLOG Africa comme outil d’intégration africaine. « Ces recommandations ne sauraient demeurer lettre morte. Nous veillerons à la mise en place, dans les délais, du comité de suivi confié au Conseil burkinabè des chargeurs, et nous accompagnerons l’élaboration de l’instrument juridique consacrant la reconnaissance officielle de TRANSLOG Africa. (…) TRANSLOG Africa doit demeurer un instrument de coopération au service d’une Afrique qui décide par elle-même et pour elle-même », a-t-il déclaré. À noter que, lors de cette édition, le symposium TRANSLOG Africa a été institutionnalisé en tant que plateforme intergouvernementale et partenariale permanente dédiée à la concertation sur les transports, la logistique et la sécurité des corridors en Afrique. Elle a pour mission d’harmoniser les cadres réglementaires et juridiques du commerce et du transport transfrontalier. Cette plateforme permettra d’accélérer la digitalisation, la cybersécurité et la résilience des corridors logistiques. Elle facilitera également le dialogue public-privé et favorisera la mobilisation des investissements pour le développement et la sécurisation des corridors régionaux. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article TRANSLOG Africa 2026 : Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: À Béjaia, un CEM se dote d’un système d’alerte absence
items.description: Le CEM Abdelmoumen, à Béjaia, innove. Ce collège a installé un système électronique d’alerte pour surveiller l’absence des élèves. Les parents des élèves absents seront aussitôt informés par SMS. « Le système de suivi des absence des élèves du CEM a été mis en service. Il permet d’informer les parents de l’absence de leurs enfants 15 minutes après le début de la première séance », a annoncé l’administration de l’établissement scolaire, sur sa page Facebook. Béjaia : un CEM se dote dun système d'alerte absence, de quoi s'agit-il ? Ce nouveau système sera soumis à une période d’expérimentation d’une semaine pour évaluer sa performance », explique la direction du CEM Abdelmoumen, accompagné d’une vidéo montrant des élèves qui passent devant l’appareil d’enregistrement conçu pour scanner les cahiers de correspondance des élèves avec le procédé code-barres. L’introduction de ce nouveau système dans une école algérienne a suscité l’enthousiasme des internautes qui ont salué cette avancée. « Une bonne initiative. J’espère qu’elle sera généralisée dans toutes les écoles, », « une bonne chose ! A encourager », « une bonne initiative surtout s’ils vont ajouter des caméras de surveillance », lit-on dans les réactions. D’autres internautes n’ont pas manqué de faire quelques remarques : « Oui c’est une très bonne initiative ! Toutefois, cela devrait se faire avec une carte d’étudiant plutôt qu’avec un cahier de correspondance… ». D’autres commentaires ont évoqué l’aspect lié au problème de la surcharge dans la plupart des établissements scolaires. « Les derniers élèves vont arriver en retard dans les classe », « ce système convient seulement aux écoles ayant moins de 400 élèves », ont relevé des internautes. L’article À Béjaia, un CEM se dote d'un système d'alerte absence est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Oti-sud/ 4e session ordinaire de la commune 2 : Les travaux consacrés en priorité à l’élaboration du budget primitif exercice 2027
items.description: Mango, 22 oct. (ATOP) – La commune Oti-Sud 2 a tenu du 14 au 19 octobre, la première partie de sa 4 e session à Takpamba, à 54 Km au sud-ouest de Mango. Les travaux ont tourné autour de l’élaboration du budget primitif exercice 2027 suivant les nouvelles orientations du ministère en charge de la Décentralisation, notamment l’étude et l’adoption de la situation financière au 30 septembre. D’autres sujets notamment la signature des contrats avec des agents de la mairie, des échanges sur des stratégies à mettre en branle pour mobiliser davantage des ressources financières, des propositions pour combler l’insuffisance des agents collecteurs dans cantons, les questions en lien avec l’assainissement, la santé, l’environnement, l’éducation dans les cantons ont été aussi abordés. Oti-sud/ 4e session ordinaire de la commune 2 Cette session se tient conformément à l’article 93 de la loi sur la Décentralisation et les libertés locales. Elle a regroupé des élus locaux, des responsables des services déconcentrés de l’Etat, des garants des us et coutumes, des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS), des responsables des associations et d’ONG et des partenaires de la commune. La session a permis d’amener des acteurs impliqués dans l’élaboration de ce budget à faire des propositions qui tiennent compte des réalités de cette communes et des directives du ministère en charge de la décentralisation. Il s’agissait d’analyser et adopter la situation financière de la commune à la fin du mois de septembre ; relever les insuffisances dans la mobilisation des recettes, recueillir des propositions pour mieux renflouer les caisses de la commune. La présentation de la situation financière révèle que les recettes des mois de juillet à septembre se chiffrent à 40.652.647FCFA, ceci, du au fait que cette commune a bénéficié au cours de cette période, du Fonds d’appui aux collectivités territoriale qui s’élevé à plus de 37 millions de FCFA. Quant aux dépenses sur cette même période, elles s’enlèvent à 3.727.395 FCFA. Le solde est excédentaire de 27.426.277FCFA. Pour le problème lié à la collecte des taxes, il est ressorti que dans cette commune, des jeunes ne veulent pas exercer le métier de collecteurs dans les cantons les quatre cantons ce qui fait chuter la mobilisation des ressources. Le préfet de l’Oti-Sud, Sambiani Fékimani Félix a félicité les élus locaux pour leur engagement à œuvrer pour le développement de cette commune. Il les a exhortés à toujours travailler en toute responsabilité et a suivre à la lettre les consignes du ministere en charge de la Décentralisaton dans l’élaboration du budget primitif qui constitue la boussole pour la commune dans la gestion éfficace des ressources disponibles. Le préfet a suggéré à la commune de mettre sur pied un comité pour gérer les questions liées à l’assainissement dans les cantons afin de se prémunir contre des maladies liées à l’insalubrité en cette période de fortes pluies. Il a réitéré sa disponibilité à accompagner cette commune dans l’atteinte de ses objectifs Le maire de la commune Oti-Sud 2, Mme Koulalo Tieba Dzigbondi a exhorté ses paires et les participants à participer activement aux travaux et à faire des propositions pertinentes pour booster le développement endogène. Mme Koulalo a insisté qu’il ait un dialogue permanent entre les populations et la mairie ajoutant que le développement de la commune incombe à tout le monde et nécessite la participation de tous. Elle a fait remarquer que sa commune est engagée à investir dans les secteurs de la santé, de l’éducation, des infrstructures socio de base, de l’assainissement et autres et nécessite la participation de tous . Elle a remercié le prefet pour ses conseils et appuis pour le dévéloppement de la commune. Les travaux ont été suspendu, en attendant le mois de décembre pour la poursuite des travaux en vue de l’adoption du budget prévisionnel. ATOP/TT/KYA

Ils représentent la Thaïlande, le Liban, le Koweït, l’Italie, la Corée du Sud et le Nigeria. Six pays représentés La cérémonie a marqué l’entrée officielle en fonction de ces diplomates au Sénégal. Il s’agit de Mme Nipa Nirannoot, ambassadrice du Royaume de Thaïlande, de M. Nadim Sourati, ambassadeur du Liban, et de M. Nayef M. Almudhaf, ambassadeur de l’État du Koweït. Zayyad Habu Abdussalam, ambassadeur de la République fédérale du Nigeria. Le Sénégal réaffirme son ouverture diplomatique À travers cette cérémonie, le Sénégal réaffirme ses relations avec des partenaires issus de plusieurs régions du monde, notamment l’Asie, le Moyen-Orient, l’Europe et l’Afrique. Cette diversité traduit la volonté du pays de maintenir des relations fondées sur le dialogue et le respect mutuel. items.title: The Limits of the Cinematic Universe
items.description: Sign up for Video Village , a new weekly newsletter in which David Sims unearths cinematic gems and brings readers into his movie obsession. When James Gunn was named a co-head of DC Studios in 2022, along with his producing partner Peter Safran, he was essentially being tasked with building a plane in midair. His remit from Warner Bros. (which owns DC Comics and its entertainment rights) was to clear away the dregs of its most recent efforts to create a cinematic superhero universe, quickly reboot things with a slate of new comic-book movies, and direct the first big entry himself, which turned out to be 2025’s Superman . The studio had spent years trying to play catch-up with Disney’s hugely successful Marvel movies, pumping out films either directed by Zack Snyder or made to suit his darker tone, and although some had hit, the overall project never seemed to find cultural ubiquity. So with Gunn (who made the hit Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy for Marvel) aboard, DC is trying again. But it’s happening as the state of genre cinema seems to be shifting away from the “cinematic universe” approach. Yes, Marvel’s still making movies, at a slightly more relaxed pace, but the many other imitators have wound down (think of Sony’s flimsy villain-focused attempts at a wider Spider-Man world, Fox’s now-collapsed X-Men universe, or failed efforts such as Universal’s “Dark Universe”). Audiences have grown savvy to the treadmill these series put them on, with each ending teasing future editions rather than providing satisfying conclusions, characters never getting happy endings, and fun cameos by past and future members of the universe substituting for actually interesting writing. Gunn and Safran, to their credit, seem somewhat self-aware about the problems that can sprout from the cinematic universe. In addition to narrative stagnation, these movies have a sort of necessary homogeneity. Part of what makes the Marvel brand “work” is that super-producer and honcho Kevin Feige has overarching creative control, so there’s a consistent tone—but also a bit of sameness to the visuals, the action, even the humor. Every movie starts filming with reshoots built in and scripts sometimes unfinished, more like the creation of a television show. So Gunn said things at DC would work differently: Movies could be green-lighted only with finished scripts , directors could put their imprimatur on whatever project they were in charge of, and entries in a given series could vary wildly in terms of genre and content. That’s why Clayface is such an interesting test case for the entire DC endeavor. The leadoff film in this universe, Gunn’s Superman , was a genuine delight, but it was very much a comic-book movie, aimed at the widest audience possible with a pretty sunny, bouncy PG-13 tone. The second effort was this summer’s Supergirl , inarguably a misfire from Craig Gillespie ( I, Tonya ) that aimed for darkly cynical but felt anonymous. Clayface is at least offering the hope of something fresh. It’s a gory, R-rated horror movie about a Batman villain who seems connected to the wider DC universe in only the slimmest of ways. The film is about an up-and-coming actor named Matt Hagen (played by Tom Rhys Harries) whose face is disfigured after a brutal attack from a gangster. He seeks experimental nanotechnology treatment to rebuild it and soon finds himself with weird “powers”—sometimes he can shape-shift into another person entirely; other times his features look like they’re melting off his skull. Clayface is essentially a visual-effects-driven body-horror movie with some impressive, gory flourishes; its only real connection to the DC Universe is that it’s set in Gotham City. I enjoyed it, while finding it rather silly, but was a little baffled by its existence in the first place. That’s because Clayface is, indeed, a member of Batman’s rogues’ gallery in comic books, a big gooey monster that the Caped Crusader occasionally does battle with. But Gunn’s new version of this world has yet to establish who will play Batman (the recent Robert Pattinson movie is not included in it), and there’s no immediate plan to do so. In a way, that’s wise (Hollywood is saturated with Batmen already), but Clayface is a minor-key work that struggles to justify itself. What worries me the most about the ongoing DC plan is that, ultimately, there may be no way to create a cinematic universe that doesn’t require a level of Marvel-like rigor. Gunn is green-lighting interesting things, and he’s had some decent success on the TV side too: The relatively gripping Lanterns is getting good ratings on HBO Max; the hilarious-sounding mockumentary The People vs. Gorilla Grodd is coming in 2027. But he’s moving at a much slower pace, which makes an oddity such as Clayface feel inessential—yes, it’s a tiny piece of a bigger landscape, but when we see only one or two works a year, that landscape is filling in too slowly for us to get invested. Marvel’s approach of total saturation was overwhelming for many, but there may be no other way to make the grander project feel worthwhile. An Essay I Enjoyed Illustration by Marine Buffard 50 Unforgettable Love Stories By The Atlantic Culture Desk Centuries before bookstores had shelves labeled ROMANCE and fictional hockey players locked eyes across the ice, the love story, with all of its attendant joys and sorrows, was an organizing principle of life—and of literature. The sentiment that another person might “complete” us enchanted both Plato and Jerry Maguire, and the search for that someone, along with the desire to understand why it can hurt so bad, has animated fiction from the beginning. The list below is an effort to name those love stories: novels, of course, but also poetry, plays, and short stories—that we consider to be the most enduring. We asked a jury of scholars, librarians, critics, and authors across genres, as well as many colleagues, to name their favorite titles that were originally written in English. We thought of our own personal touchstones, deliberated over the choices, and emerged with a group of standouts: 50 titles you won’t soon forget. Read the full article. Coming Attractions Last week I wrote about the industry turmoil going on at Warner Bros. as it merged with Paramount under the Skydance umbrella, with the storied executives Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy suddenly finding themselves out of a job after a string of misses in 2026. Well, their next opportunity might be arriving very quickly, because Netflix is the next movie studio to see turnover up top. First, “chief content officer” Bela Bajaria was axed on October 15; then her subordinate Dan Lin (who ran its film division) was informed he was out a day later. Lin had been hired in 2024 to rein in spending; a somewhat confusing New York Times profile of him this year said the studio was “done coddling Hollywood,” an oddly aggressive bit of press for a company that’s already struggling to attract top talent because of its hostility to cinema releases. Now Netflix is seemingly looking to pivot back to prestige, abandoning the belt-tightening that went on under Lin. De Luca and Abdy, who are reportedly in talks to take over, would provide an instant shot of it, given their existing relationships with big auteurs including Ryan Coogler and Paul Thomas Anderson, and they are reportedly discussing guaranteed theatrical releases, something Netflix has only just begun to tiptoe toward. It’s already happening with movies such as Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew , David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , and now the KPop Demon Hunters sequel. But could Netflix actually abandon one of its biggest tenets in search of Hollywood luster? To fill the gap being left by Warner Bros. and the merger, maybe. What Else I’m Watching The wide release most worth checking out in theaters this week is Wildwood , the epic stop-motion animated adventure directed by Travis Knight (the company’s CEO, who also directed Kubo and the Two Strings ). Wildwood , based on the first entry in Colin Meloy’s Wildwood Chronicles novels, has been in development for 15 years and in production for five, and really feels like a true labor of love. That can be said about every movie from Laika, a stop-motion studio based out of Oregon that made its name with Coraline . The films are all huge undertakings made more for artistic enjoyment than for profit, but Wildwood is especially ambitious, featuring PG-13 action and a two-plus-hour running time. Take your older kids to see and enjoy—it’s a fun modern fantasy as well as an affectionate portrait of Portland, where Knight grew up. There’s also Wicker , a sweet folk comedy that I heartily enjoyed, starring Olivia Colman as a reclusive fisherwoman who contracts a local weaver (Peter Dinklage) to make her a husband out of wicker. And indeed he does, creating a creature (Alexander Skarsgard) that looks like a handsome scarecrow and rustles romantically with every step. It has the potential to be a horror movie, but it’s actually a wry satire of patriarchal relations in medieval times (and how, in some ways, things have never changed). Colman is, as always, a true comic delight.

items.title: Sudan hunger crisis deepens as aid cuts collide with crop failure in Darfur
items.description: Cuts to food aid and a near-total crop failure are leaving displaced families and vulnerable communities struggling to find food as prices soar and malnutrition worsens. Cuts to World Food Programme (WFP) assistance threaten displaced families across Sudan, while a near-total crop failure in East Darfur has left households short of food and income. Residents of Sheairia report soaring prices, worsening malnutrition, and shortages of medicines and therapeutic food for children. In a statement to reporters following an eight-day visit to Sudan last month, the WFP’s acting executive director, Carl Skau, says the agency has the capacity to reach millions of people caught between war, displacement and worsening drought – but is running out of money. The General Coordination for Displaced People and Refugees now warns that reduced food assistance could force families to skip meals and sell their remaining possessions to survive. Adam Rijal, the coordination body’s spokesperson, told Radio Dabanga that funding shortages and cuts to WFP assistance could deprive displaced families of essential meals and force them to adopt increasingly desperate coping strategies, including withdrawing children from school, selling their remaining possessions, and reducing the number and size of meals. Children, women, older people, and people with disabilities face particular risks of malnutrition and disease, he said, calling on donors and international institutions to close the funding gap and ensure food assistance reaches those most in need. Distribution of seeds to small farmers in the Um Shujaira area of ​​Sha’iriya locality, East Darfur – July 2026 (Photo: Supplied) Failed harvests deepen food insecurity The warning comes as residents of Sheairia locality in East Darfur report a near-total failure of the agricultural season, sharply higher food prices, and shortages of medicines for people and livestock. Resident Babiker Ishaq told Radio Dabanga that farmers had harvested almost nothing of their main crops, including groundnuts, millet, sorghum, and okra. The losses have deprived households of a crucial source of food and income, leaving some unable to find enough to eat amid the absence of humanitarian assistance. A sack of millet costs about SDG 350,000 when paid for through bank transfers, while a sack of sorghum costs a similar amount, Ishaq said. A pound of onions costs around SDG 4,500, a bottle of cooking oil between SDG 13,000 and SDG 14,000, and a pound of sugar about SDG 4,000 when paid for through bank transfers. He said deductions on transfers through the Bankak app, which he estimated at 40% in some cases and 50% in others, further reduce the money available to families for essential purchases. Malnutrition and medicine shortages The food crisis is also affecting children and pregnant women. Ishaq said pregnant women were unable to obtain adequate diets and children were suffering from malnutrition, while supplies of therapeutic food were limited. He called for increased supplies to treat malnourished children and urgent deliveries of medicines and medical supplies. Livestock are also at risk because of shortages of veterinary medicines. Ishaq reported illnesses among cattle, horses, and donkeys, adding that about six or seven children had reportedly been bitten by dogs suspected of having rabies. A rabies treatment injection costs about SDG 300,000, he said, putting it beyond the reach of many families. Calls for urgent humanitarian assistance Rijal called on donors and international institutions to maintain food assistance, strengthen nutrition and food security programmes, and prioritise the worst-affected areas. He also urged the authorities to ensure safe, unhindered access for aid deliveries and called for an end to the war and a humanitarian truce to allow relief to reach civilians. Ishaq appealed to humanitarian and health organisations to provide food, medicines, therapeutic nutrition supplies, and veterinary care to protect both residents and the livestock on which many families depend. Compétitivité du secteur privé: l’État recense les difficultés des entreprises du Pôle nord
items.description: Le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan a ouvert, mardi 20 octobre, à Saint-Louis, deux jours de concertation territoriale avec les entreprises stratégiques du Pôle nord. Cette rencontre a pour objectif d’identifier les contraintes qui freinent l’investissement privé et de dégager des solutions concrètes pour renforcer la compétitivité des entreprises locales, stimuler la création d’emplois et contribuer à la mise en œuvre de la « Vision Sénégal 2050 ». Saint-Louis – Donner davantage de place au secteur privé dans la transformation économique du pays. C’est l’ambition des concertations territoriales organisées, les 20 et 21 octobre, à Saint-Louis, par le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, en collaboration avec les autorités administratives. Les échanges réunissent les entreprises stratégiques autour de leurs difficultés, de leurs perspectives de développement et des mesures attendues des pouvoirs publics. Pour Khoudia Lèye Diouf, adjointe au gouverneur de Saint-Louis chargée du développement, cette initiative offre un cadre privilégié d’expression aux acteurs économiques de la région. « C’est l’occasion d’écouter les entreprises intervenant dans la région, pour qu’elles puissent revenir sur les difficultés auxquelles elles sont confrontées, mais également formuler leurs recommandations », a-t-elle expliqué. Les contributions recueillies doivent permettre de mieux orienter les décisions publiques et de conforter les ambitions de la « Vision Sénégal 2050 ». Au-delà du diagnostic, les autorités veulent donner une traduction opérationnelle aux préoccupations exprimées par les chefs d’entreprise. Aziz Fall, coordonnateur à la Direction générale de la Coopération, des financements extérieurs, du développement du secteur privé et des partenariats, insiste sur la nécessité de passer de l’identification des acteurs économiques à la recherche de solutions adaptées à leurs besoins. « On ne va pas résoudre tous les problèmes en deux jours, mais on va montrer qu’il y a une nouvelle dynamique qui s’enclenche », a-t-il souligné. Cette démarche doit, selon lui, permettre de distinguer les difficultés pouvant être résolues rapidement de celles nécessitant des études techniques, des réformes ou des investissements structurants. M. Fall met également l’accent sur les opportunités offertes par le développement du secteur extractif, notamment l’exploitation du gaz. L’enjeu est que les entreprises locales puissent prendre leur place dans les chaînes de valeur générées par cette activité. « Cette dynamique ne laissera aucune chaîne de valeur en rade, y compris le secteur des hydrocarbures », a-t-il assuré, réaffirmant l’engagement de l’État à accompagner le développement du secteur privé sans discrimination sectorielle. Inscrites dans la Stratégie nationale de développement du secteur privé et de promotion de l’investissement 2025-2029, ces concertations ciblent particulièrement les chaînes de valeur du riz, du tourisme et de l’oignon, considérées comme prioritaires dans le Pôle nord. Les travaux doivent déboucher sur une synthèse des contraintes, des recommandations hiérarchisées et un plan d’action destiné à améliorer l’environnement des affaires. Des rencontres entre entreprises et administration sont également prévues, ainsi que des présentations de projets à fort potentiel de création de richesses et d’emplois. La deuxième journée est consacrée aux travaux thématiques, à l’examen des projets d’investissement et aux visites d’entreprises ciblées. Les conclusions attendues doivent alimenter une feuille de route de suivi-évaluation afin d’assurer la continuité des engagements pris. De son côté, le Président-directeur général de Sénégal Agrogreen, Adama Ba, a souligné les principales difficultés auxquelles sont confrontées les entreprises locales. Elles concernent, dit-il, le foncier, la fiscalité et le financement. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Festival des Terres du Nazinon : La culture au service de la paix et du développement
items.description: La deuxième édition du Festival des Terres du Nazinon s’est ouverte le 19 octobre 2026 à Manga, autour du thème « Unité, Culture, Paix et Jeunesse ». Les organisateurs ambitionnent de faire de ce rendez-vous un cadre de cohésion sociale, de promotion du patrimoine culturel et de création d’opportunités économiques pour les populations du Nazinon. Le Festival des Terres du Nazinon entend renforcer sa contribution à la valorisation du patrimoine culturel et au développement local. La promotrice, Denise Koudougou/Oulon, a réaffirmé sa volonté de faire de cette manifestation un rendez-vous fédérateur, ouvert aux communautés et tourné vers la jeunesse. Placée sous le thème « Unité, Culture, Paix et Jeunesse » , cette édition entend promouvoir la diversité culturelle comme un facteur de rapprochement entre les populations. Pour la promotrice, le festival se veut un espace de rencontre entre les générations et les communautés, mais aussi une tribune d’expression pour les artistes, les artisans et les entrepreneurs culturels. « Nous réaffirmons notre volonté de faire de la culture un instrument d’unité, de paix et de développement », a-t-elle déclaré. À travers les prestations artistiques, les expositions et la promotion des produits locaux, les organisateurs souhaitent contribuer à la transmission des traditions, à la valorisation des talents et au renforcement des liens entre les filles et les fils de la région. La première édition du Festival des Terres du Nazinon avait mobilisé plus de 50 000 participants, selon le patron de l’événement, Jacques Sosthène Dingara. Pour cette deuxième édition, la manifestation passe de quatre jours à une semaine d’activités, traduisant la volonté des organisateurs de consolider les acquis et d’accroître son rayonnement. Au-delà de la célébration culturelle, le festival entend contribuer au développement économique du territoire. La promotrice a notamment insisté sur le potentiel touristique de la région du Nazinon, qui dispose, selon elle, de richesses naturelles, historiques et culturelles encore insuffisamment connues et valorisées. Les sites touristiques, les savoir-faire artisanaux et les expressions culturelles constituent, à ses yeux, des leviers susceptibles de renforcer l’attractivité de la région, de créer des opportunités économiques et d’offrir de nouvelles perspectives à la jeunesse.
